a MUHAMMAD TARIO AFRIDI. J.- Through the instant writ petition, filed under Article 199 of the constitution, the petitioners have prayed for the following relief:

"On acceptance of instant writ petition, the august Court may be pleased to; Set-asidc and quash the FIR No' 02 dated: 09.09'2024 lodged in Police Station Anti-Conuption Bannu under Sections 409,419,420, 468, 471of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 and 5(2) Prevention of Corruption Act, 7947, and Restrain the respondents permanently from harassing, humiliating and publicly ridiculing the petitioners and their family members through delibcrate campaign and by maliciously prosecuting them in false and bogus cases like the one in hand, and / or Grant any othcr remedy deemed appropriate may also be granted in favour of the Petitioner."

2. Briefly, facts of the case, as set forth in the instant writ petition, are that on 19.08.2024, Mr. Abdur Rahim, Circle Offrcer, Anti-Corruption' Bannu' submitted a sorrce report to the Director of Anti-Comrption Establishment, 1ll.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, through the Assistant Director Crimes, stating therein that Dilawar Khan and Sadiq Dilawar Khan were allegedly selling govemment land by developing a housing scheme under the name "Central Provincial Elite community Residentia cPEC Colony," thereby causing a loss of millions of rupees to the public exchequer, and sought permission for conducting an open inquiry in order to investigate the matter and obtain statements and relevant record. Permission to conduct the inquiry was accorded and communicated vide Letter No . 5s45l\CL,dated Peshawar the 2l'08'2024' bearing the subject:
"OPEN ENQUIRY NO.71I2024-REV: AGAINST DILAWAR KIIAN AND SADIQ DILAWAR AND CONCERNED STAFF OF Rf,VENUE DEPARTMENT DISTRICT BANNU,,withdirectionstofinalizethesamepositivelywithinonemonth.

3. The Circle Officer, Anti-Comrption, Bannu' upon conclusion of the enquiry, found that 39-Kanal of land bearing old Khasra Nos' 2593 arrd 2594' corresponding to new Khasra Nos' 5824 and 5827 situated in Mouza Bharat' Bannu, comprising a water channel (Khwar)' allegedly belonging to the Provincial Govemment' had been illegally occupied and unlawfully incorporated into and made part of the aforesaid society' consequently' he submitted his report recommending registration of a criminal case against Taj Mali Khan, the then Sub-Registrar, Bannu' Dilawar Khan son of Ghulam Muhammad, and Humayun Dilawar and Sadiq Dilawar' sons of Dilawar Khan' residents of Kafshi Khel, Bannu' 4. Accordingly, a criminal case vide FIR No'2' dated 09'09'2024' under Sections 4Og, 4lg, 420, 468, and 471of the Pakistan Penal Code' 1860' read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act' 7947 ' was registered at Police Station Anti-Comlption' Bannu' Thereafter' the leamed Judicial Magistrate-Il, Bannu, upon an application moved by the Circle Officer' Anti- Com.rption, Bannu, issued warrants for the arrest of the present petitioners' directing that the same shall remain in force until the arrest and production of the petitioners before the Court' 5. Feeling aggrieved by the registration of the aforesaid criminal case' the petitioners, having no other adequate and efficacious remedy available under ?
the law, have approached this Court through the instant constitutional petition, seeking quashment of the FIR in question.

6. Arguments were heard and the record was perused with the valuable assistance of the leamed counsel for the petitioners, the learned Additional Advocates-General, and the learned Assistant Advocate-General for the State. 7 . Leamed counsel for the petitioners submitted that Petitioner No' l , namelyDilawarKhan,expiredanaturaldeathduringthependencyofthe instant writ petition on 19.01.2026. The leamed Additional Advocates-General, the leamed Assistant Advocate-General, and Raza Ullah, DSP, also confirmed thedeathofDilawarKhan.Consequently,boththecriminalproceedingsas wellastheproceedingsbeforethisCourt,insofarastheyrelatetoPetitioner No.l, stand abated.

8. Leamed counsel further submitted that Petitioner No'2' namely Humayun Dilawar' is a serving Judicial Officer' presently holding the post of District&SessionsJudge(BPS-21)inthelslamabadDistrictJudiciaryarrdis working under the administrative control and supervision of the Honourable IslamabadHighCourt.HefurthersubmittedthatPetitionerNo'3'namelySadiq Dilawar, is serving as Senior Investigation Officer (BPS-17) in the Provincial Ombudsman Secretariat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa' Peshawar' g.

It was argued that Petitioner No'1, namely deceased Dilawar Khan' was owner in possession of certain landed properry situated in Mouza Bharat' Tehsil Kakki,DistrictBannu,whichwassubsequentlytransferredbyhiminfavourof Cenhal Provincial Elite Community Residentia (CPEC)' an approved housing scheme, through various mutations and registered sale deeds' It was further contended that, out of the said transactions' the transfers effected vide Registered Deed/lVasiqa Nos'l179 and 1180' Bahi No'1' Jild No'163 dated l6.O5.2[22,were subsequently disputed by the Anti-Corruption Establishment (ACE), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, allegedly at the behest of the Provincial Govemment, acfuated by mala fide intent and ulterior motives, purportedly to seek vengeance on account of the conviction of the former Chairman ofPTI in a criminal case, which conviction had been recorded by Petitioner No'2 in his V capacity as Additional Sessions Judge/Presiding Officer ofthe trial court upon conclusion of the proceedings.

10. Leamed counsel for the Petitioners contended that the impugned FIR is the outcome of mala fide, arbitrariness, and a deliberate abuse of the process of law, originating from a self-generated and fabricated Source Report dated 1g.08.2024, on the basis whereof, Open Enquiry No' 7112024 was initiated' It was argued that the enqulry proceedings were merely cosmetic in nature' as the entire record reflects only a single progress report dated 30.08.2024, while neither any witness nor the Petitioners were examined during the course of the enquiry.LeamedcounselfurthersubmittedthatRegisteredDeedsNos.llT9 and 1180, both dated 15.06.2022, remain valid, intact, and operative to date, andthattheownershipandpossessionofPetitionerNo.l(nowdeceased)over the property in question have never been disputed by any person or authority' includingtheGovemment.Despitethis,thesaidregistereddeedsweremade the sole basis for the registration of the impugned FIR by the Anti-Com'rption Establishment (ACE)' It was further argued that' in highly suspicious circumstances, the so-called final report, legal opinion, approval by the DirectorACE,andregishationoftheimpugnedFlRwereallprocessedand finalized in undue haste on the same day, i'e', 09'09'2024' 11. Learned counsel vehemently argued that the Director, ACE, vide letter dated29.10.2025, referred the matter to the Deputy Commissioner' Bannu' who thereafter constituted an eight-member committee comprising revenue and executive officers/offrcials to conduct a detailed inquiry' Upon thorough examination of the revenue record, registration documents, and demarcation proceedings, the Committee concluded that Registered Deeds Nos' 1179 and ll80,executedpursuanttodecreedated30.03.lgS0,alongwithconsequential Mutation Nos. 18232 and 19329' were lawful' valid' and fully justified' 12. Leamed counsel further submitted that approval/Nocs in favour of CPEC Residentia were granted by the Deputy Commissioner' Bannu' as ChairmanoftheDistrictScrutinyCommitteecomprisingseniorofficersofall relevant departments, as well as by TMA Kakki' Bannu, after inviting public objections through newspapers and social media in 2023 ' It was further t/ contended that additional clearances were also issued by the concerned Highway, Agriculture, Canal and EPA authorities. Leamed counsel emphasized that none of the said authorities has ever objected to, withdrawn, or cancelled theNoCssogranted.ItwasfurtherarguedthattheDeputyCommissioner, Bannu, in his capacity as District collector and Dishict Regishation officer, hasexpresslyvalidatedandendorsedtheregistereddeedsinquestion,whilethe registered deeds and consequential mutations continue to remain valid and operative till date.

13.Leamedcounselfurthersubmittedthattheveryfoundationoftheinquiry andtheconsequentregistrationoftheFlRislegallyuntenable,beinginclear violation of the relevant provisions of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Anti- Comrption Establishment Rules, 1999' According to the leamed counsel' RespondentNo.2,whileservingasanAdditionalsessionsJudge'Islamabad' was deliberately targeted, and the respondents' acting in haste' with mala fide intent, and in complete disregard of the applicable legal requirements and goveming rules, unlawfully caused the registration of the FIR against petitioner No. 2, as well as his father and brother' on the basis of an illegal and unauthorized inquiry.
While concluding their arguments, the leamed counsel contended that

14. the impugned FIR, being founded uPon a fabricated source report' a subsequently manipulated inquiry, and illegal proceedings' constitutes a clear abuse of the process oflaw and is, therefore' liable to be quashed' 15. Conversely, Ieamed Additional Advocate-General' Mr' Muhammad Inam Yousafzai, submitted that the impugned FIR was the outcome of a verified source report and a preliminary inqulry conducted in accordance with the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Anti-Comrption Establishment Rules' 1999' during which, documentary record prima facie disclosed cognizable offences relating to fraudulent transfer of land through manipulation of revenue record and misuseofajudicialdecree.Hefurthercontendedthatdespitebeingduly summoned, the Petitioners willfully abstained from joining the inquiry and' therefore, cannot allege denial of due process at this stage' It was vehemently contendedthattheinstantpetitionhasbeeninstitutedsolelytoobstructalawful criminal investigation, despite the settled principle of law that constitutional jurisdiction ought not to be invoked to stifle criminal proceedings at a nascent stage where the FIR discloses cognizable offences' 16. The learned Additional Advocate-General, while elaborating upon the aforesaid submissions, advanced the following contentions:

a) That during the inquiry, revenue record obtained from the concemed departmentsrevealedthatdeceasedDilawarKhanhadinstifutedaCivil suittitted..DilawarKhan-V-GhulamHussainandanother,'No.36211 instituted on 02.09.1976' in respect of Khasra Nos' 2603' 2604' arrd 2605. The leamed Senior Civil Judge, Bannu, vide judgment and decree dated 30.03.1980, granted permanent injunction against dispossession fromthesaidKhasranumbers.However,thesaiddecreewas e subsequently misused to claim ownership over different Khasra Nos' 5824 and 5827 measuring 39-Kanal' which neither formed part of the suit nor were covered by ihe dec.ee, and were admittedly jointly owned by Mahazi Malikan.

b) That Mutation No' 5140 dated 24'01'2023 was attested in Mahazi Malikan,MouzaBharat,infavourofDilawarKhan(PetitionerNo'1)on the basis of Registry/WasiqaNo' 1179' Bahi No' 1' Jild No' 613' dated 15.06.2022, which is ex facie defective' as it does not disclose the requisite particulars of the Khata and Khasra numbers of the alienated property. Leamed Additional Advocate-General further contended that' on it. ,t .ngtt of the said Registry/Wasiqa No' I 179 dated 15'06'2022' Dilawar Khan subsequently transferred' through Mutation No' 5141 dated 24.01.2023, larrd measuring 39 Kanals comprised in Khasra Nos' 5824 and 5827 situated in Mouza Bharat' Bannu' in favour of Central Provincial Elite community Residentia (CPEC), which mutation was attested on the basis of the subsequent Registry/wasiqa No' 1 180 dated 15.06.2022, despite the admitted position that the aforesaid Khasra numberswerenevffthesubjectmatterofthelitigationinquestion. c) That such deliberate misapplication and misuse of the judicial decree constitutes a serious abuse ofthe legal process and' on its face' gives rise to penal liability under the applicable provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code and the Prevention of Comrption Act' d) That the Petitioners' reliance on the report of the Deputy Commissioner' Bannu, is misconceived and irrelevant' as the report pertains to Khasra Nos. 5813, 5818,5820, and 5823, whereas the FIR specifically concems Khasra Nos. 5824 and 5827. The report is, therefore, factually distinguishable and legally inapplicable to the present contoversy. Moreover, it merely reflects an administrative opinion and neither establishes lawful ownership nor explains the Petitioners' chain of title over the disputed land. consequently, the report neither validates the impugned transactions nor absolves the Petitioners of criminal liability. e) That the subject property forms part of Shamilat-e-Deh (communal land)

and, under Section 6 of the Transfer of Properry Act' 1882 read with Sections 125, 126 and 127 of the Land Revenue Act' 1967 is nontransferable and incapable of alienation in favour of private individuals' Any transaction or mutation effected in violation thereof is void ab initio, without lawful authority, and non est in the eye of law' ThatthecontentionthatPetitionerNo.lhasexpiredandPetitionersNo.2 & 3, being merely wibresses to the deeds' cannot be held liable for the alleged ofi.n"., is legally misconceived and untenable. Petitioners No.2 U { *" not only beneficiaries of the transaction but also the legal heirs of Petitioner No.l. Upon his death, any rights and liabilities arising therefrom devolved upon them; therefore, they cannot escape liability on the hyper-technical plea of being mere witnesses to the deeds' While concluding their submissions, the learned Additional Advocates- General and the Assistant Advocate-General prayed that the present Writ Petition,beingdevoidofmeritandnotmaintainable'bedismissed'andthatthe investigation in FIR No.02 dated 09'09'2024 be allowed to proceed shictly in accordance with law, along with any other relief deemed just and proper in the facts and circumstances ofthe case' 18. In light of the submissions of both sides' the record was minutely examined. Before addressing the merits of the case' it is appropriate to frst consider the petitioners' objection that the FIR was registered in violation of the provisions of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Anti-Comrption Establishment Rules, 1999, and is therefore liable to be quashed on this ground alone' 19. For adjudication of the legal question as to whether the initiation of the preliminary inquiry and the consequent registration of the impugned FIR offend Rules 3 and 4 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Anti-Comrption Establishment Rules, 1999, read with Rule 9 thereof, it is necessary to examine the allegations ?
forming the basis of the inquiry alongside the said provisions to determine their legality in accordance with law.

20.Theoriginalrecordofthecasewasrequisitioned,produced,andretained by the court for scrutiny and adjudication of the matter. The record reveals that, on the basis of a source report dated lg.O8.2L24,permission to conduct an open inquiry was granted within two days vide Letter No' 5545/ACE dated 21.08.2024. The inquiry was thereafter concluded within 19 da whereupon the Circle Officer reported that 39-Kanal of land comprised in Khasra Nos' 5824 and 5827, situated in Mouza Bharat, Bannu, constituting a water channel (Khwar) allegedly owned by the Provincial Govemment' had been illegally occupied and incorporated into the housing scheme in question' He consequently recommended registration of a criminal case against Taj Mali Khan, the then Sub-Registrar, Bannu, Dilawar Khan son of Ghulam Muhammad, and Humayun Dilawar and Sadiq Dilawar' sons of Dilawar Khan' notwithstanding that neither Taj Mali Khan nor Humayun Dilawar had been named in the original source rePort' Consequently' FIR No'2 dated 09'09'2024 was registered at Police Station Anti-Comrption' Bannu' under Sections 409' 41g,420,468 and 471 PPC, read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Comrption Act, 1947,against the aforesaid four (04) persons' 21. Leamed counsel for the petitioners alleged that Imran Khan Niazi was convicted on 05.08.2023, under Section 174 of the Elections Act' 2017' by Petitioner No. 2, namely Humalun Dilawar' Additional Sessions Judge' Islamabad(West),inacomplaintfiledbytheDistrictElectionCommissioner' Islamabad, under Section 190 of the Elections Act' 2077 ' for making a false declaration regarding assets acquired by way of gifts from Toshakhana' He was sentenced to simple imprisonment for three years and a fine of Rs'100'000/- on 05.08.2023. It was' therefore, argued that the registration of the present FIR was motivated by, and stemmed from' the grievance arising out of the aforesaid judgment of conviction. Leamed counsel further submitted that the said conviction and its circumstances remained unrebutted' as no argument to the contrary was advanced bY the State' 22. In light of the foregoing facts, objections, and Rules 3 and 4 of the KhyberPakhtunkhwaAnti-ComrptionEstablishmentRules,lggg,readwith Rulegthereof,thisCourtconsidersitnecessarytoexaminewhetherthe prescribed legal requirements were duly complied with' or whether any deviation therefrom occurred, in the initiation of the inquiry and the subsequent regishation of the FIR.

23. Record reflects that a source report dated 19.08.2024 was prepared by AbdulRahim,CircleOfficer,Anti-Corruption'Bannu'Recordalsorevealsthat neitherHuma1unDilawarnorTajMaliKhan'Sub-Registrar'Bannu'was named or referred to in the said source report. lt is further noteworthy that withinaspanofmerelytwo(02)daysfromthepreparationofthesourcereport, theDirectorAnti-ComrptionEstablishment'KhyberPakhtunkhwa'accorded approvalfortheinitiationofaninquiry,andwithinthenextnineteen(19)days, anFlRcametoberegisteredagainstHumayunDilawar(withoutdescribinghis ? status as an Additional Sessions Judge)' his father and brother' as well as the Sub-Registrar.

The foregoing sequence of events' when examined in juxtapositionwiththejudgmentofconvictionrenderedagainstlmrarrKhan Niazi, former Chairman PTI, prima facie' suggests an unusual degree of expedition in the initiation and culmination of the proceedings, particularly when the source report, which formed the foundation of the proceedings' containednoallegations,referenceormaterialagainstHumayunDilawar' Additional Sessions Judge, Islamabad, who was subsequently nominated as an accused.

24. In the context of these events' the record of the Anti-Comrption Establishment was examined, from which it became evident that the source report was neither submitted on the complaint of any person' nor was any source of information disclosed therein' For this reason' the summons/notices issued by the Circle Officer, Anti-Comrption' were also examined so that a proper assessment could be made regarding the faimess or bias' as well as the good faith or mala fide intent, involved in the investigation of the case' 25. The record reveals that a service notice dated 'Og '2024 was issued to Haji Dilawar Khan and Sadiq Dilawar for the purpose of recording their statements, requiring their appearance on 05.09'2024, however, no summons or notice was ever issued to Humayun Dilawar, notwithstanding the fact that the allegations against him were identical in nature to those leveled against his brother sadiq Dilawar. Both brothers were shown as attesting witnesses to the two registered deeds through which the Shamilati land was transferred allegedly by means of fraud. In these circumstances, the omission of Humayun Dilawar, Additional sessions Judge, Islamabad, from the inquiry proceedings appearsdeliberateandlendsconsiderablesupporttotheinferencethathis exclusion was intended to avoid compliance with the requisite legal formalities, whichcouldotherwisehaveimpededordelayedtheregistrationoftheFlR.

26. It is noteworthy that the source report did not contain even a passing referencetoHumaytrrrDilawareitherbynameordesignation.However,inthe finalreportdated0g.0g.2024,itwasalleged,onthebasisofthesourcereport' that Dilawar Khan and his sons, Sadiq Dilawar and Humayun Dilawar, had illegally occupied government land, established a "Central Provincial Elite Community Residentia CPEC Colony", thereon' and sold plots' thereby deriving unlawful financial gains amounting to hundreds of thousands of rupees. The final report further reveals that the Circle Officer' Anti-Comrption Establishment (ACE) concluded that Humayun Dilawar and Sadiq Dilawar' in collusion with the Sub-Registrar Bannu, had caused wrongful gains amounting tomillionsofrupeestothemselvesandtheirfather'Consequently'he recommended the registration of a criminal case' On the very same day' the Director Anti-Comrption Establishment (ACE) Khyber Pakhtunkhwa accorded approval, whereupon, FIR No'2, dated 09'09'2024' under Sections 409' 419' 420,468 and 471ofthe Pakistan Penal Code' 1860' read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Comrption Act, 1947 ' was registered at Police Station Anti- ComrPtion, Bannu.

27. The question that arises for consideration is whether the Circle Officer andtheDirectorofACEKhyberPakhtunkhwaweregenuinelyunawarethat Mr.HumayunDilawarwasthesameAdditionalsessionsJudge,Islamabad, who had presided over the Toshakhana case and had convicted and sentenced Mr.ImranKhanNiazi'theformerChairmanPTl,tothreeyears,imprisonment '/ along with a fine; or whether, with fuIl knowledge of his identity and official status, they deliberately omitted his name and designation from the source report with a view to facilitating the registration of a criminal case against him' Itfurtherrequiresdeterminationwhethersuchomissionwasactuatedby extraneous considerations, including political pressure or influence' and whether the criminal proceedings were instituted without compliance with the mandatoryrequirementsoflaw,therebyvitiatingtheentireprocessonaccount ofmalafides,arbitrariness,andanulteriormotiveaimedatvictimisingand taking revenge against him?

28. The record reflects that the petitioners' through Miscellaneous Application No. 166-8/2025, placed on record an attested copy of Daily Diary Report No. 5 dated 06.09.2024 of Police Station ACE' Bannu' The said DDR reveals that a notice was served upon the Circle Officer' ACE' by Mt' Humayun Dilawar, in his capacity as a Judicial Officer' through his counsel' and that this fact was duly communicated by the concemed ACE official to the higher authorities of the department' Admittedly' the aforesaid Daily Diary Report dated 06.09.2024 predates FIR No'2 dated 09'09'2024' which clearly demonstratesthattheofficialsoftheAnti-ComrptionEstablishmentwere already aware of Mr. Humayun Dilawar's status as a Judicial Officer before the registration of the FIR.

29. Apart from the foregoing, it is an undisputed fact that Imran Khan Niazi isthefourderandformerChairmanofPakistanTehreek-e-Insaf(PTI)'a political party that has remained in government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for a considerable period. It is equally a matter of common knowledge that numerous legal proceedings involving Mr' Imran Khan attracted extensive media attention and public interest, with widespread reporting regarding the forums before which such Proceedings adjudication.

pending and the stages of their 30. In these circumstances, particularly in an era characterized by pervasive electronic, print, and social media coverage' coupled with unprecedented public access to information, the assertion that officials of the Anti-Comrption EstablishmentwereunawirrebothofMr.HumayunDilawar,sstatusasaBPSwere t2 20 Judicial Officer and of the Toshakhana proceedings during the course of the inquiry appears difficult to reconcile with the surrounding facts and circumstances. Such a position, on its face, raises legitimate questions regarding the diligence, objectivity' and bona fides of the inquiry process' prima facie, the conduct in question appears incompatible with the faithful and diligent discharge of offrcial duties and tends to suggest an exercise of authority coloured by mala considerations.

examlne, tn fides rather than guided by lawful and bona fide 31. In view of the foregoing discussion, this Court considers it appropriate to the light of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Anti-Comrption Establishment Rules, 1999, the legality and validity of the inquiry conducted by the Anti-comrption Establishment and the FIR subsequently registered pursuant thereto. For ease of reference and proper appreciation of the controversy involved, Rules 3, 4, arrd 9 of the said Rules are reproduced hereunder:
Rute-3. Preliminary/Open enquiries against Public Servants'---(l)
Preliminary inquiries and investigation against public servants shall be initiated by the Establishment on complaints received from Govemment' Head of Departments or other reliablc sources'

(2) 'Ihe Director shall initiate preliminary/open enquiries in order to ascertain the identity of the complaint or informer and geniuses of the comPlaint or information' (3) It shatl be incumbent on rhe Head of concerned Departmcnt/Office to provide the relevant record required in connection with enquiries/investigations as soon as a request is made by the Establishment' Provided the enquiry against the District Co-ordinate Officers in the Districts, Secretaries to the Provincial Government' Head of Attached O.pu.tr*nt, and other officers in BPS-19 and above shall be initiated by the Director with prior permission of the Chief Secretary' Rule-4. Registration of cases/arrest of accused"--(1)

Criminal cases shall be registered by the Bstablishment under the Prevention of Comrption Act 1947 and under such sections of Pakistan Pcnal Code' as have been set forth in the Schedule to the Ordinance' (2) Criminal cases shall be registered against accuscd public servants under th" *.itten orders of the off,icers mentioned below:l3 ?

(a) Public Servants in BPS-I8 & below - - Director (b) Public Servants in BPS-19 & above - - ChiefSecretary ProvidedthatforPublicservantsinBPS-lgandabove,theChief Secretary, before according permission, may, in his discretion, get the case examinedbyaJudicialofficerspeciallyappointedintheEstablishmentand Administration Department of Government of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for the purpose.

Provided further that no prior permission shall be required for registration of a case against a public servant caught as a result of a trap arranged by the Establishment under the supervision of a Magistrate or any other Gazetted Ofhcers authorised by the District and Sessions Judge or in his absence by an Additional District and Sessions Judge' in the act of committing an offence specified in the schedule to the Ordinance' In such a case, a report shall immediately be made to the Chief Secretary' the Administrativc Secretary and immediate superior of the public servant concemed if he is in BPS-16 and above, and to thc appointing authority and immediate superior officer if the public servant is in BPS-15 and below' (3) If the compctent authority under sub-rule (2) above decides not to register a case, he shall record reasons therefor' (4) While making a request for registration of a case against the accused prUti" ,"*unt, a simultaneous request may be made by the Establishment to the authorities specified below if the arrcst is so required during the investigation:

(a) Public Servants upto BPS-16 - - Director (b) Public Servants in BPS-17 & above - - ChiefSecretary Provided that no prior pcrmission shall be necessary for the arrest of a public servant caught as a result ofa trap as mentioned in the last proviso to sub-rule (2) of Rule-4' Rule-9. Wherc Senior Public Servant are involvcd alongwith Junior Public Servants.---For the purpose of initiation of preliminary/open enquiri"s, registration of cases, dropping the cases after investigation' or referring the same for departmental action' or taking a decision with regard to prose-cution, if more than one public servant is involved' the competent uutho.ity for thesc decisions shail b" the one which is in case of public servants in the highest BPS' when confronted with the aforesaid rules, the leamed Additional
32. Advocate General (AAG) contended that, since the name of Humayun Dilawar t4 ?

was not included in the inquiry proceedings, the Director Anti-comrption, being the competent authority under the law, had validly accorded permission to initiate an inquiry against the sub-Registrar, Baruru. He further argued that, upon completion of the inquiry and in light of the incriminating material collected therein, the registration ofan FIR against a Judicial officer in BPS-20 was fully in consonance with the letter and spirit of the law' 33.ThesubmissionsadvancedbytheleamedAdditionalAdvocateGeneral, though seemingly atffactive at first glance, do not withstand close scrutiny and are founded on a misconstruction of the relevant statutory framework' A cumulativereadingofRules3,4andgleavesnoroomforambiguitythatthe DirectorAnti-Comrptionisnotvestedwiththeauthorityeithertoinitiatea preliminary/open inquiry against, or to order the registration of a criminal case against, a public servant in BPS-19 or above' Under the proviso to Rule 3' any inquiry against such officers can only be initiated by the Director after obtaining prior permission of the Chief Secretary' Likewise' Rule a(2)(b) expressly mandates that registration of a criminal case against a public servant in BPS-19 and above requires the written approval of the Chief Secretary' exceptinthelimitedcaseofatrapoperation,whichadmittedlyisnotattracted in the present matter. F urthermore, Rule 9 provides that where officers of different grades are involved in the same matter' the competent authority shall be determined with reference to the officer holding the highest BPS' Therefore' onceanofficerinBPS.lgorabovewasimplicated,theentirematterfellwithin theexclusivedomainoftheChiefSecretary,andtheDirectorAnti-Comrption could neither independently authorize the inquiry nor direct registration of the FIR. Any action taken in derogation of these mandatory requirements is withoutlawfulauthorityandsuffersfromajurisdictionaldefect'renderingthe proceedings legally unsustainable' 34. The Court shall now proceed to examine the record conceming the factualmatrixofthecaseinthelightofthesubmissionsmadebytheparties. Therefore, each objection and the corresponding reply shall be considered and decided separately and in detail as follows;

TheleamedAAGcontendedthatCivilsuitNo.362l|,ir|ed..Dilawar Khan v. Ghulam Hussain and another", instituted on 02'09'1976, was merely a suit for permanent injunction relating to Khasra Nos' 2603' 2604, and 2605, seeking protection against dispossession' The suit was decreed by the leamed Senior Civil Judge, Bannu, on 30'03'1980' According to the leamed AAG, a Wasiqa was subsequently registered on 15.06.2022 vide Registry No. 1179, Bahi No' 1, Jild No' 613' on the basis of the said decree. The Wasiqa is alleged to be ex facie defective' as it does not disclose the requisite particulars of the Khata and Khasra numbers of the alienated property' Consequently' Mutation No' 5140 dated 24.01.2023, attested in favour of Dilawar Khan (Petitioner No. 1)

from the Mahazi Malikan of Mouza Bharat on the basis of the said Wasiqa, is also stated to be illegal' a. From a perusal of the record, it is conclusively clear that in the above-mentioned judgment, the Court held in paragraphs 8 and 9 that during cross-examination, Dilawar Khan stated that in the yeat 197l,he had purchased the land under the possession of the adjoining co-owners (Mahazi Malikan)' The Court further observed that according to the Khasra Girdawari placed on record' the suit land stood in the possession of Dilawar Khan through tenants and concluded that he had proved his case beyond reasonable doubt.

b. In these circumstances, the contention of the leamed AAG that the decree was merely an injunction decree and that the subsequent Wasiqa/registered deed was the result of fraud or deception owing to the non-mentioning of Khasra numbers is not sustainable for two reasons. Firstly, it is not the case of the Govemment that the property in question is State land' The Govemment' therefore' Iackslocusstanditochallengetheproprietaryrightsofan individualonthegroundthatthepropertymaybelongtoother private persons. Secondly, although the registered Wasiqa does not expressly mention the Khasra numbers' it specifically refers to the litigation from which the hansaction emanates' wherein the relevant Khasra numbers are duly mentioned' Moreover' the corresponding revenue entries have neither been annulled nor set aside, and no legal proceedings have been initiated against the revenueoffrcialsresponsibleforrecordingorattestingthesame.
